title: We Need to Talk About Covid, Part 1

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做 DJ 的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, in a recent poll, the Times set out to understand how Americans were thinking about the pandemic as they headed into a third year.
sentences.zh: 今天，在最近的一项民意调查中，《纽约时报》试图了解美国人在进入疫情第三年时对疫情的看法。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, David Leonhardt, about what the poll ended up revealing about how ready or not the country is to have a new conversation about how to go on living.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事大卫·莱昂哈特谈了谈，这次民调揭示了美国对于如何开启关于“与病毒共存”的新对话，究竟准备好了没有。

sentences.en: With the virus.
sentences.zh: 与病毒共存。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 1 月 26 日，星期三。

sentences.en: David, you have been at The New York Times for two decades, covering economics, overseeing all of our Washington coverage, writing an op-ed column.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你在《纽约时报》工作了二十年，报道过经济新闻，负责过我们所有的华盛顿报道，还写过评论专栏。

sentences.en: But this is actually your first appearance on The Daily because as we were creating this show, you were off creating your own new approach to the news,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这是你第一次在《每日新闻》亮相，因为在我们创办这档节目时，你正在忙着开创自己报道新闻的新方式，

sentences.en: which was a newsletter called The Morning.
sentences.zh: 也就是那份名为《早间》的通讯。

sentences.en: And it's become a very important part of how many people understand the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 它已经成为许多人理解疫情的一个非常重要的渠道。

sentences.en: You have taken a very data-driven approach to helping readers understand where we are or where we aren't at any given moment in these past two years.
sentences.zh: 在过去两年里，你一直采用非常注重数据的方法，帮助读者了解我们在任何特定时刻所处的境地。

sentences.en: And all of which is to say, welcome to The Daily, and I'm sorry it has taken so long.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，欢迎来到《每日新闻》，很抱歉让你等了这么久。

sentences.en: Well, it's great to be here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里，迈克尔。

sentences.en: As a longtime listener of New York Talk Radio, I'm reminded of the phrase, longtime listener, first-time caller, or first and long.
sentences.zh: 作为纽约谈话电台的长期听众，我想起了一句老话：长期听众，首次来电，或者叫“首发长传”。

sentences.en: First and long.
sentences.zh: 首发长传。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: So, the reason we want to talk to you today is because, as part of your coverage of the virus, David,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们今天想和你谈谈，是因为作为你对病毒报道的一部分，大卫，

sentences.en: you decided to commission a public opinion poll about Americans' views of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你决定委托进行一项关于美国人对疫情看法的民意调查。

sentences.en: So, just to start, what was your goal with this poll?
sentences.zh: 那么，首先，你做这项民调的目标是什么？

sentences.en: Why a pandemic poll?
sentences.zh: 为什么要做疫情民调？

sentences.en: And why now?
sentences.zh: 为什么是现在？

sentences.en: Because it seems like we might be at a turning point with COVID.
sentences.zh: 因为看起来我们可能正处于新冠疫情的转折点。

sentences.en: And I think there are a few reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几个原因。

sentences.en: So, first of all, a lot of people have put a lot of effort into avoiding getting COVID.
sentences.zh: 首先，很多人为了避免感染新冠付出了巨大的努力。

sentences.en: But Omicron makes that a lot harder because it's just so contagious.
sentences.zh: 但奥密克戎让这一切变得困难得多，因为它实在太容易传播了。

sentences.en: And so, there are people out there who tried really hard to avoid COVID and are now sort of saying, you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人曾经非常努力地避免感染新冠，现在却在说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I just have to admit that I'm probably going to get it and be okay with that.
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认，我可能还是会感染，我对此也只能接受。

sentences.en: And that's understandable because the second thing about Omicron is that it tends to be milder than earlier versions of the virus.
sentences.zh: 这是可以理解的，因为关于奥密克戎的第二点是，它往往比早期版本的病毒更温和。

sentences.en: It can still be severe for people who are not vaccinated and for a small number of people who are immunocompromised or very elderly.
sentences.zh: 对于未接种疫苗的人，以及少数免疫功能低下或非常年长的人来说，它仍然可能很严重。

sentences.en: But for the vast majority of people, if you are vaccinated and you get Omicron, you are not going to get very sick.
sentences.zh: 但对于绝大多数人来说，如果你接种了疫苗又感染了奥密克戎，你通常不会病得很重。

sentences.en: In the United States, at least, we now have virtually universal access to vaccines.
sentences.zh: 至少在美国，我们现在几乎实现了全民疫苗接种。

sentences.en: Anyone who's old enough and wants to be vaccinated can now be vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 任何达到年龄要求且愿意接种的人现在都可以接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And so, when you sort of put all this together, you realize, wait a second, we might be at a pivot point with COVID in which it goes from being this horrible, deadly,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你把这一切放在一起看时，你会意识到，等等，我们可能正处于新冠疫情的转折点，它正从那种可怕、致命、

sentences.en: life-dominating pandemic to something that is more endemic.
sentences.zh: 主宰生活的全球大流行，转变为一种更具地方性的疾病。

sentences.en: To something that looks more like things that we deal with all the time without shutting down daily life, like the flu.
sentences.zh: 变成一种像流感那样，我们无需停止日常生活就能应对的常态。

sentences.en: And so, given all that, we wanted to do a poll, and we wanted to go out there and say to Americans, how are you feeling about COVID right now?
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，我们想做一项民调，想去问问美国人：你现在对新冠有什么感觉？

sentences.en: How worried are you still about getting sick?
sentences.zh: 你对生病还有多担心？

sentences.en: What do you think governments should do in response to COVID?
sentences.zh: 你认为政府应该采取什么措施来应对新冠？

sentences.en: So, we asked Morning Consult, which is a survey firm, to go out and conduct a national poll, and they did so.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们请调查公司 Morning Consult 进行了一项全国性民调，他们照做了。

sentences.en: They interviewed more than 4,400 Americans all across the country from different demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 他们采访了全国各地 4400 多名来自不同人口统计学群体的美国人。

sentences.en: And they basically said, how are you thinking about COVID now?
sentences.zh: 他们基本上问的是：你现在怎么看待新冠？

sentences.en: How are you thinking about what the future of COVID is going to be?
sentences.zh: 你认为新冠的未来会怎样？

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: what you're saying is that this is a statistically sound effort to take the temperature of the American public on exactly how it's thinking about COVID at this moment that might or might not be a pivot in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，这是一项统计学上严谨的努力，旨在探查美国公众在这一时刻对新冠的真实看法，而这一时刻可能是疫情的一个转折点。

sentences.en: And given that question you had going into this poll, are we at a turning point?
sentences.zh: 考虑到你在进行这项民调时提出的问题，我们是否正处于转折点？

sentences.en: Tell us about what you found.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你的发现。

sentences.en: The first thing I'd say is there is no one thing we found.
sentences.zh: 首先我想说，我们的发现并不是单一的。

sentences.en: Americans' attitudes toward COVID differ based on all kinds of factors, the same way our attitudes on all sorts of subjects differ, often quite starkly.
sentences.zh: 美国人对新冠的态度因各种因素而异，就像我们在各种议题上的态度往往存在巨大分歧一样。

sentences.en: But I would say that even though I've spent most of the last two years writing about COVID and reporting about it, there were still parts of this poll that surprised me.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，尽管过去两年我大部分时间都在撰写和报道新冠疫情，但这项民调中仍有一些部分让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And those parts, I do think, raise some questions about exactly how we're going to pivot and when we're going to pivot,
sentences.zh: 我认为这些部分确实引发了一些关于我们将如何转变以及何时转变的问题，

sentences.en: whether we're weeks away from a pivot or still many months away from a pivot.
sentences.zh: 无论是几周后还是几个月后才会出现转折。

sentences.en: And the three issues that really raised those questions in my mind were, one, about how people of different age groups are thinking about COVID risk.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，真正引发这些问题的三个议题是：第一，不同年龄段的人如何看待新冠风险。

sentences.en: The second was about how people with different vaccination status are thinking about COVID risk.
sentences.zh: 第二，不同疫苗接种状况的人如何看待新冠风险。

sentences.en: And the third one was how people are thinking about schools right now and how they should be operating.
sentences.zh: 第三，人们现在如何看待学校以及学校应该如何运作。

sentences.en: So, let's start with what you just said were surprising views of the pandemic by age group.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从你刚才提到的关于不同年龄段对疫情的惊人看法开始吧。

sentences.en: What did the poll find?
sentences.zh: 民调发现了什么？

sentences.en: I think this is really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点非常引人注目。

sentences.en: We found a striking degree of similarity among older and younger people about how worried they were about getting sick from COVID.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，老年人和年轻人对于感染新冠的担忧程度惊人地相似。

sentences.en: So, 17% of people aged 65 and above said they were very worried about getting sick from COVID.
sentences.zh: 65 岁及以上的人群中，有 17% 表示非常担心感染新冠。

sentences.en: And 23% of people 18 to 34 said they were very worried.
sentences.zh: 而在 18 至 34 岁的人群中，有 23% 表示非常担心。

sentences.en: So, younger people were slightly more likely to say that they were very worried about getting sick from COVID than older people.
sentences.zh: 所以，年轻人比老年人更有可能表示非常担心感染新冠。

sentences.en: Now, when you look across the whole poll, I don't want to make too much of small differences.
sentences.zh: 现在，纵观整个民调，我不想过度解读这些微小的差异。

sentences.en: What I would say is that the degree of worry is quite similar among younger people and older people.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，年轻人和老年人的担忧程度非常接近。

sentences.en: And the reason that's so surprising is that we know scientifically the risk is not similar.
sentences.zh: 而这之所以令人惊讶，是因为从科学角度来看，风险并不相似。

sentences.en: It's extremely different.
sentences.zh: 风险差异极大。

sentences.en: It's much higher for older people.
sentences.zh: 老年人的风险要高得多。

sentences.en: It's so much higher that three quarters of all deaths in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 高到什么程度呢？美国四分之三的死亡病例，

sentences.en: have been among people aged 65 and older.
sentences.zh: 都发生在 65 岁及以上的人群中。

sentences.en: COVID is overwhelmingly mild for younger people.
sentences.zh: 新冠对年轻人来说绝大多数是轻症。

sentences.en: And yet, older people and younger people essentially look at the risks and give extremely similar answers, even though the reality is that the risks are very different.
sentences.zh: 然而，老年人和年轻人看待风险的方式却基本一致，给出的答案也极其相似，尽管现实情况是风险差异巨大。

sentences.en: Well, given all that, what would drive young people to be as anxious as older people about COVID?
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于这一切，是什么驱使年轻人像老年人一样对新冠感到焦虑呢？

sentences.en: Because the data shows that's just not in line with the scientific risk.
sentences.zh: 因为数据显示这与科学风险并不相符。

sentences.en: How do you start to explain that?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: I start to explain it by saying political ideology has to be a big part of this.
sentences.zh: 我的解释是，政治意识形态在其中必然占据了很大比重。

sentences.en: And we see that repeatedly in the poll.
sentences.zh: 我们在民调中反复看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So across most demographic groups, COVID attitudes really aren't that different.
sentences.zh: 在大多数人口统计学群体中，对新冠的态度其实并没有那么大的差异。

sentences.en: Men and women don't have very different COVID attitudes.
sentences.zh: 男性和女性对新冠的态度并没有太大不同。

sentences.en: Different racial groups don't have very different COVID attitudes.
sentences.zh: 不同种族群体对新冠的态度也没有太大不同。

sentences.en: The rich, the middle class, and the poor don't have very different COVID attitudes.
sentences.zh: 富人、中产阶级和穷人对新冠的态度也没有太大不同。

sentences.en: Who does have very different COVID attitudes?
sentences.zh: 那么谁对新冠的态度有很大不同呢？

sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人。

sentences.en: Radically different COVID attitudes.
sentences.zh: 他们对新冠的态度截然不同。

sentences.en: And I think the most fascinating way to see this is to look at the poll by both partisanship and by age.
sentences.zh: 我认为观察这一现象最迷人的方式，就是同时从党派和年龄两个维度来看待这项民调。

sentences.en: It's really kind of remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: So if you look across either Republicans or Democrats, there's almost no difference in how people assess their own personal risk by age.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察共和党人或民主党人，会发现人们对自身风险的评估几乎没有年龄差异。

sentences.en: So old Republicans are roughly as worried as young Republicans.
sentences.zh: 年长的共和党人和年轻的共和党人一样担心。

sentences.en: Old Democrats are roughly as worried as young Democrats.
sentences.zh: 年长的民主党人和年轻的民主党人一样担心。

sentences.en: And as we've talked about, that's just not scientifically rational.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，这在科学上是不理性的。

sentences.en: But when you separate out Democrats and Republicans, the gap is enormous.
sentences.zh: 但当你把民主党人和共和党人分开来看时，差距是巨大的。

sentences.en: It is so big that older Republicans are significantly less worried about getting sick than younger Democrats.
sentences.zh: 差距大到年长的共和党人对感染的担忧程度显著低于年轻的民主党人。

sentences.en: Only 47% of Republicans who are 65 and older say they are worried about getting sick from COVID.
sentences.zh: 在 65 岁及以上的共和党人中，只有 47% 表示担心感染新冠。

sentences.en: 70% of Democrats between the ages of 18 and 34 are worried about it.
sentences.zh: 而在 18 至 34 岁的民主党人中，有 70% 表示担心。

sentences.en: So when you look at all this,
sentences.zh: 所以当你审视这一切时，

sentences.en: what you end up seeing is that people's attitudes toward risk doesn't seem to be driven by rational thought or scientific evidence so much as it seems to be driven by political belief.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，人们对风险的态度似乎并非由理性思考或科学证据驱动，更多是受政治信仰驱动。

sentences.en: David, it's interesting you used the word rational.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你用了“理性”这个词，很有意思。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying that there's kind of a politically infused irrationality to these divergent views of the old and the young when it comes to the risk of COVID.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是在说，当谈到新冠风险时，老一代和年轻一代这些截然不同的观点中，存在一种政治注入的非理性。

sentences.en: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是这个意思。

sentences.en: And I think there is.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为确实如此。

sentences.en: I think you see it with Republicans who are refusing to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我认为你在那些拒绝接种疫苗的共和党人身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And I think you see it with Democrats who are really struggling to imagine a future in which COVID isn't a dominant part of our life.
sentences.zh: 我也认为你在那些难以想象没有新冠的生活的民主党人身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I always tell people, don't put too much stock into any one poll.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉人们，不要太迷信任何单一的民调。

sentences.en: But it's not just our poll that's finding this.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是我们这一项民调发现了这一点。

sentences.en: It's poll after poll.
sentences.zh: 这是一份又一份民调的结果。

sentences.en: As the folks at Gallup said, Republicans are consistently underestimating COVID risks and Democrats are consistently overestimating COVID risks.
sentences.zh: 正如盖洛普公司的人所说，共和党人一贯低估新冠风险，而民主党人则一贯高估新冠风险。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市的“交易手册峰会”上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Okay, so David, tell us about the second big surprising finding from this poll of Americans about the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 好的，大卫，告诉我们关于这项美国疫情民调的第二个重大惊人发现。

sentences.en: You said it was around the question of vaccine status.
sentences.zh: 你说过这与疫苗接种状况有关。

sentences.en: What did the poll find?
sentences.zh: 民调发现了什么？

sentences.en: I found this remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很了不起。

sentences.en: The more protected you are from COVID, the more worried you are about your own personal risk across groups.
sentences.zh: 你受到的新冠保护越好，你对个人风险的担忧就越强烈，这一趋势在各群体中都存在。

sentences.en: So what that means is that the people who express the greatest worry about how at risk they are to COVID illness are the boosted.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，那些对自身感染新冠风险表示最担忧的人，正是那些接种了加强针的人。

sentences.en: The vaccinated but not boosted are not as concerned about how exposed they are to risk as the boosted are.
sentences.zh: 接种了疫苗但未接种加强针的人，对自身风险的担忧程度不如接种了加强针的人。

sentences.en: And the least worried are the unvaccinated.
sentences.zh: 而最不担心的是未接种疫苗的人。

sentences.en: Now, on some level, I get this, right?
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我理解这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: If you were worried, you would go get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 如果你担心，你就会去接种疫苗。

sentences.en: But the fact that having been vaccinated or having not been vaccinated doesn't change people's views is really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 但接种过疫苗或未接种疫苗这一事实并没有改变人们的观点，这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: So if you told me that the people who were more worried about this would go get vaccinated, I would say, well, of course, that's what they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你告诉我，那些更担心的人会去接种疫苗，我会说，嗯，当然，他们肯定会这么做。

sentences.en: That just only makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这完全合乎逻辑。

sentences.en: But the idea that unvaccinated people continue in many cases not to express much concern and that boosted people continue to express high levels of concern in many cases,
sentences.zh: 但未接种疫苗的人在许多情况下仍然不表达太多担忧，而接种了加强针的人在许多情况下仍然表达出高度担忧，

sentences.en: not everyone, of course, but in many cases, that's really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 当然不是所有人，但在许多情况下，这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: I think it's important to focus for a second on just how small the risk is for most boosted people in the case of Omicron.
sentences.zh: 我认为有必要花点时间关注一下，对于大多数接种了加强针的人来说，奥密克戎带来的风险其实非常小。

sentences.en: We're still waiting for the data to confirm this, but there's a lot of indication that if you are boosted, Omicron appears to present less risk than the flu.
sentences.zh: 我们还在等待数据证实这一点，但有很多迹象表明，如果你接种了加强针，奥密克戎带来的风险似乎比流感还低。

sentences.en: So if you think about yourself, if you're a boosted person, I'm a boosted person, and you think about what you are going to do today and the risk you're going to expose yourself,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想自己，如果你是一个接种了加强针的人——我也是——当你考虑今天要做什么以及要暴露在什么风险中时，

sentences.en: By my calculation, looking at data on how many people go to ERs and die, I almost certainly expose myself to more risk by setting foot in a vehicle today,
sentences.zh: 根据我的计算，查看人们去急诊室和死亡的数据，我今天出门坐车所面临的风险，几乎肯定比新冠带给我的风险要大，

sentences.en: vehicle crashes kill about 40,000 Americans every year, than COVID presents to me.
sentences.zh: 车祸每年导致约 4 万名美国人死亡，这比新冠对我的威胁要大。

sentences.en: But that's not how boosted people are thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 但接种了加强针的人并不是这样想的。

sentences.en: They're not thinking, oh, this morning when I get up, there's a small risk that I might choke.
sentences.zh: 他们不会想：哦，今天早上起床时，我有很小的风险会噎住。

sentences.en: There's a small risk that I might be in a car accident.
sentences.zh: 我有很小的风险会遭遇车祸。

sentences.en: They're focusing overwhelmingly on this tiny COVID risk.
sentences.zh: 他们绝大多数的注意力都集中在这个微小的新冠风险上。

sentences.en: And the flip side of that is unvaccinated people who really are at mortal risk from COVID are often just dismissive of it.
sentences.zh: 而另一面是，那些真正面临新冠致命风险的未接种疫苗者，往往对此不屑一顾。

sentences.en: So this is another pretty staggering gap between what the scientific data tells us and the level of anxieties you're finding from people in this poll.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是科学数据告诉我们的事实与你在民调中发现的人们焦虑程度之间的一个巨大差距。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, we don't fully understand what is driving these gaps, but it's clear that political belief is driving a significant portion of it.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们并不完全理解是什么导致了这些差距，但很明显，政治信仰在其中起到了很大作用。

sentences.en: And this isn't just what people are saying when they're contacted by a poll.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是人们在接受民调时所说的话。

sentences.en: Look at the statistics on vaccination.
sentences.zh: 看看疫苗接种的统计数据。

sentences.en: According to the most recent numbers we have, fewer than 10% of Democratic adults are unvaccinated.
sentences.zh: 根据我们掌握的最新数据，民主党成年人中未接种疫苗的比例不到 10%。

sentences.en: The most recent numbers for Republicans, it's about 40% of Republican adults are not vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人的最新数据是，约 40% 的共和党成年人未接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And so there's this enormous gap, not just in attitudes, but in behavior to how people are responding to this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因此，不仅在态度上，而且在人们应对这场大流行病的行为上，都存在巨大的差距。

sentences.en: Partisanship has become a dominant way that we think about COVID the same way partisanship is dominant in our thinking on abortion and guns and climate change and so many other issues.
sentences.zh: 党派之争已成为我们思考新冠疫情的主导方式，就像党派之争在堕胎、枪支、气候变化以及许多其他议题上主导了我们的思维一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What's interesting about what you're saying, David, is that it's not only showing that partisanship is dictating whether people get vaccinated, which I think we did know.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你所说的有趣之处在于，它不仅表明党派之争决定了人们是否接种疫苗，我想这一点我们确实已经知道了。

sentences.en: It's also showing that even those who do get vaccinated, who do believe the science that shows vaccines are protective,
sentences.zh: 它还表明，即使是那些确实接种了疫苗、确实相信科学证明疫苗具有保护作用的人，

sentences.en: are still having a pretty high level of fear that suggests they actually don't really feel protected.
sentences.zh: 仍然有相当高的恐惧感，这表明他们实际上并没有真正感到受到保护。

sentences.en: And that's counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这与直觉相悖。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you believe the science, you should go get the vaccine because all the science says the vaccines are very safe and very effective at preventing serious COVID illness.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你相信科学，你就应该去接种疫苗，因为所有的科学都表明，疫苗在预防新冠重症方面非常安全且有效。

sentences.en: But let's focus on that second beat just for a second.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先关注一下第二点。

sentences.en: The science says vaccines are very effective at preventing serious COVID illness.
sentences.zh: 科学表明，疫苗在预防新冠重症方面非常有效。

sentences.en: So if you believe the science, it doesn't argue only for getting vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你相信科学，它不仅支持接种疫苗。

sentences.en: It also argues for living your life in a way that reflects that you've been vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 它还支持以一种反映你已经接种疫苗的方式来生活。

sentences.en: Now, I know that many boosted people will say, look, I'm not worried about myself.
sentences.zh: 我知道，许多接种了加强针的人会说，看，我不担心我自己。

sentences.en: I'm worried about infecting others.
sentences.zh: 我担心的是传染给别人。

sentences.en: And that shows an admirable concern for others.
sentences.zh: 这表现出了一种令人钦佩的对他人的关怀。

sentences.en: The thing to remember is that those other people have also had the opportunity to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 但要记住的是，那些人也同样有机会接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And the data suggests that for vaccinated people, Omicron looks a lot like other common respiratory illnesses.
sentences.zh: 数据表明，对于接种过疫苗的人来说，奥密克戎看起来很像其他常见的呼吸道疾病。

sentences.en: As we've said, it's usually mild, but it can be rough on elderly or immunocompromised people.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，它通常很温和，但对老年人或免疫功能低下的人来说可能会很严重。

sentences.en: So the question becomes, if COVID is starting to look like a regular respiratory virus,
sentences.zh: 所以问题就变成了，如果新冠开始看起来像一种普通的呼吸道病毒，

sentences.en: is it rational for us to treat it like something completely different and to disrupt our lives in all these big and consequential waves?
sentences.zh: 我们把它当作完全不同的东西来对待，并以所有这些巨大且影响深远的方式扰乱我们的生活，这合理吗？

sentences.en: And I think this is very important to emphasize.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点非常重要，必须强调。

sentences.en: The steps we have taken to minimize the spread of COVID had big benefits.
sentences.zh: 我们为最大限度减少新冠传播所采取的措施带来了巨大的好处。

sentences.en: They saved a huge number of lives.
sentences.zh: 它们挽救了大量生命。

sentences.en: But they also have had enormous costs.
sentences.zh: 但它们也付出了巨大的代价。

sentences.en: And by almost any measure, American society just isn't functioning very well right now.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎从任何衡量标准来看，美国社会目前运转得并不好。

sentences.en: Violent crime has soared, and it started soaring shortly after the pandemic began.
sentences.zh: 暴力犯罪激增，而且在大流行开始后不久就开始激增。

sentences.en: There was just this interesting study out that showed Americans' blood pressure had gone up.
sentences.zh: 最近有一项有趣的研究显示，美国人的血压升高了。

sentences.en: Many people have just been working from their homes.
sentences.zh: 许多人一直都在家里工作。

sentences.en: Mental health problems have gone up.
sentences.zh: 心理健康问题增加了。

sentences.en: Drug overdoses have soared.
sentences.zh: 药物过量死亡人数激增。

sentences.en: And so the idea that we've all isolated ourselves and we've sublimated these normal human interactions, that has had huge costs.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们都自我隔离并压抑了这些正常的人际互动，这种想法付出了巨大的代价。

sentences.en: And so I think the thing we need to grapple with is, at what point do the costs of pandemic precautions outweigh the benefits?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要努力解决的问题是，大流行预防措施的代价在什么时候会超过其收益？

sentences.en: I think this very naturally leads us to the final category of views that you mentioned at the beginning of our conversation, which is around schools.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很自然地引出了你在对话开始时提到的最后一类观点，即关于学校的问题。

sentences.en: So what did the poll show about that?
sentences.zh: 那么民调对此有何显示？

sentences.en: It's another area where you said the results were surprising.
sentences.zh: 这是你提到的结果令人惊讶的另一个领域。

sentences.en: Let's start with an area of partisan agreement, because like a lot of people, I sometimes get exhausted by all of our partisan divides.
sentences.zh: 让我们从党派达成共识的领域开始，因为和许多人一样，我有时会对我们所有的党派分歧感到疲惫。

sentences.en: So one place where we really see partisan agreement are on these questions of, are the changes to schools damaging kids?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们确实看到党派达成共识的一个地方是关于这些问题：学校的改变是否在损害孩子？

sentences.en: And you see a clear majority of Democrats and a clear majority of Republicans and a clear majority of independents say yes.
sentences.zh: 你会看到绝大多数民主党人、绝大多数共和党人和绝大多数独立人士都表示同意。

sentences.en: The difference is what Democrats and Republicans think we should do about schools.
sentences.zh: 区别在于民主党人和共和党人认为我们应该如何处理学校问题。

sentences.en: And so here you see a clear majority of Democrats being in favor of taking significant extra precautions in order to reduce the spread of Omicron.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以看到绝大多数民主党人赞成为减少奥密克戎的传播而采取重大的额外预防措施。

sentences.en: So we ask people, do you support or oppose transitioning students from in-school to online because of Omicron?
sentences.zh: 所以我们问人们，你支持还是反对因为奥密克戎而将学生从校内学习转为在线学习？

sentences.en: And 65% of Democratic voters say yes.
sentences.zh: 65%的民主党选民表示支持。

sentences.en: 61% of Republican voters say no.
sentences.zh: 61%的共和党选民表示反对。

sentences.en: What I think is particularly notable here is the internal contradictions for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里特别值得注意的是民主党内部的矛盾。

sentences.en: Democrats, they are simultaneously saying, look, we're really worried about remote school, right?
sentences.zh: 民主党人，他们同时在说，看，我们真的很担心远程教学，对吧？

sentences.en: We're worried about the educational loss for our kids.
sentences.zh: 我们担心孩子们的教育损失。

sentences.en: We're worried about the costs in terms of socialization.
sentences.zh: 我们担心社交方面的代价。

sentences.en: We're worried about the emotional and psychological costs for them.
sentences.zh: 我们担心他们所承受的情感和心理代价。

sentences.en: And there's huge evidence that they're right to be worried about all that.
sentences.zh: 而且有大量证据表明，他们担心这一切是正确的。

sentences.en: Children appear to be in crisis right now by any number of measures.
sentences.zh: 从许多衡量标准来看，孩子们似乎正处于危机之中。

sentences.en: And yet Democrats also say they are in favor of moving schools online in order to reduce the spread of Omicron.
sentences.zh: 然而，民主党人也表示，他们赞成为减少奥密克戎的传播而将学校转为在线教学。

sentences.en: So the question is, are those costs justified given that Omicron tends to be mild, not only for vaccinated adults, but also for unvaccinated children?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，考虑到奥密克戎不仅对接种疫苗的成年人，而且对未接种疫苗的儿童往往都很温和，这些代价是否合理？

sentences.en: The rates of long COVID seem to be low also for kids based on the evidence that we have.
sentences.zh: 根据我们现有的证据，儿童患长期新冠的比例似乎也很低。

sentences.en: Whereas Republicans are being pretty consistent.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人则相当一致。

sentences.en: They're saying both, we think closing schools hurts our kids and we want schools to remain open as a result.
sentences.zh: 他们既说，我们认为关闭学校会伤害我们的孩子，因此我们希望学校保持开放。

sentences.en: And I think there really is a question of what is the scientific evidence that justifies the idea of shutting schools,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为确实存在一个问题，即有什么科学证据能证明关闭学校的想法是合理的，

sentences.en: given how bad the effects are for kids in a country where vaccines are universally available and the effects are mild in children.
sentences.zh: 考虑到在一个疫苗普遍可及且儿童症状温和的国家，这对孩子的影响有多糟糕。

sentences.en: And I've yet to hear a science-based answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 我还没有听到对这个问题的科学回答。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so how do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Look, this pandemic has been really difficult for people.
sentences.zh: 看，这场大流行对人们来说确实非常困难。

sentences.en: It's caused a horrific amount of death and it's dominated daily life for two years.
sentences.zh: 它造成了可怕的死亡人数，并主导了过去两年的日常生活。

sentences.en: And we also live in a country where people's political identities are often really core to who they are.
sentences.zh: 而且我们生活在一个人们的政治身份往往是其核心的国家。

sentences.en: And so those two things have sort of combined, the terribleness of the pandemic and the strength of people's political identities.
sentences.zh: 所以这两件事结合在了一起，大流行的可怕和人们政治身份的强烈。

sentences.en: And we've seen Republicans adopt this attitude in which downplaying COVID to the point of saying falsely that vaccines don't matter, that's become central to who they are.
sentences.zh: 我们看到共和党人采取了这样一种态度：淡化新冠，甚至错误地声称疫苗无关紧要，这已成为他们身份的核心。

sentences.en: In some cases, it's cost Republicans their lives.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这让共和党人付出了生命的代价。

sentences.en: On the flip side, we've seen Democrats who've reacted to that and who've reacted to really a lot of misinformation out there from President Trump, from conservative media.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们看到民主党人对此做出了反应，也对特朗普总统和保守派媒体散布的大量错误信息做出了反应。

sentences.en: And they've said, hey, we're going to go in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嘿，我们要走相反的方向。

sentences.en: We are going to take this virus absolutely as seriously as we can.
sentences.zh: 我们要尽可能严肃地对待这种病毒。

sentences.en: We view our masks not only as a form of protection, but as a statement that we're progressives and that we believe in science.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅把口罩视为一种保护形式，还将其视为一种声明，表明我们是进步派，我们相信科学。

sentences.en: And I think on both sides, it's ended up going beyond where the science should allow it to go.
sentences.zh: 我认为在双方，这最终都超出了科学所允许的范围。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you're inclined to see this moment, Omicron starting to peak, infections going down, as a pivot point,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你倾向于将这一时刻——奥密克戎开始达到顶峰，感染人数下降——视为一个转折点，

sentences.en: it feels like what this poll has taught us is that the strength of Americans' political identifications
sentences.zh: 感觉这次民调告诉我们的是，美国人政治认同的强度，

sentences.en: and how much that's bound up in the way they view the pandemic is a pretty big obstacle to everyone pivoting at the same time or in any way or shape in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 以及这与他们看待大流行的方式结合得有多紧密，是每个人同时或以任何形式向同一方向转变的一个相当大的障碍。

sentences.en: So what's going to be necessary for the country to actually pivot on the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 那么，国家要真正实现大流行病的转折，需要什么？

sentences.en: I think it's worth remembering that Americans do still agree on many things.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得记住的是，美国人在许多事情上仍然达成共识。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they agree on is the fact that eventually we will get beyond COVID.
sentences.zh: 他们达成共识的事情之一是，我们最终会超越新冠。

sentences.en: We ask people that question.
sentences.zh: 我们问过人们这个问题。

sentences.en: Do you think we'll get to a point in which we live with COVID without it disrupting daily life?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们是否会达到一种与新冠共存而不扰乱日常生活地步？

sentences.en: And a majority of both Republicans and Democrats said, yes, they do expect that to happen.
sentences.zh: 大多数共和党人和民主党人都表示，是的，他们确实期待这种情况发生。

sentences.en: And so I guess that then raises the question of, well, how is that going to happen and when is it going to happen?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这就引出了一个问题，好吧，这会如何发生，什么时候会发生？

sentences.en: And I think the how is there are two points to consider here.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于“如何”这一点，有两个方面需要考虑。

sentences.en: Nothing would be more helpful for us moving on from COVID than increasing the number of Americans who are vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比增加接种疫苗的美国人数量更能帮助我们走出新冠了。

sentences.en: These vaccines are amazing and they really do transform this terrible virus into something that's overwhelmingly manageable.
sentences.zh: 这些疫苗非常了不起，它们确实将这种可怕的病毒变成了某种绝大多数情况下可控的东西。

sentences.en: So if something could happen to change that and get more of the millions and millions of Republicans who remain unvaccinated to get vaccinated,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果能发生什么改变这一点，让数以百万计仍然未接种疫苗的共和党人去接种疫苗，

sentences.en: that would lead to less stress on our hospitals.
sentences.zh: 那将减轻我们医院的压力。

sentences.en: And our hospitals are really stressed now because the Omicron wave is not yet over.
sentences.zh: 我们的医院现在压力很大，因为奥密克戎浪潮还没有结束。

sentences.en: It would mean our nurses and our doctors wouldn't have to work so hard all the time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们的护士和医生不必一直那么辛苦地工作。

sentences.en: It would mean people who need medical treatment for other reasons could more often get it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着那些因其他原因需要医疗救治的人能更经常地得到治疗。

sentences.en: And it would reduce the number of Americans who are dying each day from this virus.
sentences.zh: 这将减少每天因这种病毒而死亡的美国人数量。

sentences.en: I think the second thing is, and this is on the Democratic side, at what point do we manage to say, okay, I can accept a very small risk that is not a zero risk?
sentences.zh: 我认为第二点是，这在民主党方面，我们在什么时候能说，好吧，我可以接受一个非常小的风险，而不是零风险？

sentences.en: And I think we see a lot of Democrats struggling with that question.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们看到许多民主党人在这个问题上挣扎。

sentences.en: I think that's why so many Democrats are in favor of shutting schools relatively quickly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么这么多民主党人赞成相对迅速地关闭学校。

sentences.en: I think that's why we see so many Democrats resistant to the idea of offices reopening, because they see these risks, which are not zero, but have gotten very, very small.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么我们看到这么多民主党人抵制办公室重新开放的想法，因为他们看到了这些风险，虽然不是零，但已经变得非常非常小。

sentences.en: And they have said, oh, that's still too large for me.
sentences.zh: 他们却说，哦，这对我来说仍然太大。

sentences.en: And they aren't ready yet to weigh the costs of our precautions with the costs of the virus.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有准备好权衡我们的预防措施代价与病毒的代价。

sentences.en: They aren't really putting on a scale, okay, the damage that these disruptions are doing to children, the damage they're doing to vulnerable communities,
sentences.zh: 他们并没有真正放在天平上衡量，好吧，这些干扰对儿童造成的损害，对弱势群体造成的损害，

sentences.en: the damage they're doing to our mental health with the costs of COVID in the current moment.
sentences.zh: 对我们心理健康造成的损害，与当前新冠带来的代价相比如何。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What you're really saying, it seems, David, is that even if Americans say they want to learn to live with COVID, that they want to make a pivot, it's going to be really hard,
sentences.zh: 大卫，你真正想说的是，即使美国人说他们想学会与新冠共存，他们想做出转变，这也会非常困难，

sentences.en: because making that pivot is going to require many Americans to change how they identify themselves vis-a-vis the virus,
sentences.zh: 因为做出这种转变将需要许多美国人改变他们相对于病毒的自我认同，

sentences.en: to change something quite essential about how they think about the pandemic and themselves.
sentences.zh: 改变他们看待大流行和自身方式中非常本质的东西。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We're never going to get to a morning where COVID is dead.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会迎来新冠彻底消失的那一天。

sentences.en: There is always going to be a potential future variant.
sentences.zh: 未来总会有潜在的变异株。

sentences.en: There's always going to be some small risk of something bad happening from COVID.
sentences.zh: 新冠总会有一些导致不良后果的小风险。

sentences.en: There's always going to be uncertainty about long-term symptoms for a small percentage of people who get it.
sentences.zh: 对于一小部分感染者来说，长期症状总会有不确定性。

sentences.en: These are real questions.
sentences.zh: 这些都是现实的问题。

sentences.en: They're serious questions.
sentences.zh: 它们是严肃的问题。

sentences.en: They need scientific attention.
sentences.zh: 它们需要科学关注。

sentences.en: But that's not the same as saying, okay, we're going to remain in some version of the mode that we've been in for the last two years over the course of the rest of our lives.
sentences.zh: 但这并不等同于说，好吧，我们要余生都保持过去两年我们所处的那种模式。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so the question is, how do we balance the very real risks and costs of COVID with the very real risks and costs of disrupting life in order to respond to COVID?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，我们如何平衡新冠带来的非常现实的风险和代价，与为了应对新冠而扰乱生活带来的非常现实的风险和代价？

sentences.en: David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 大卫，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the Times reported that a handful of Democratic governors in states like Pennsylvania and Colorado
sentences.zh: 周二，《泰晤士报》报道称，宾夕法尼亚州和科罗拉多州等州的少数民主党州长

sentences.en: are beginning to adopt a new approach to the virus that moves them closer to their Republican counterparts by avoiding measures like school shutdowns and mask mandates.
sentences.zh: 开始采取一种新的病毒应对方法，通过避免学校停课和口罩令等措施，使他们更接近共和党同僚。

sentences.en: The change, the Democratic officials told the Times, reflects their belief that more and more Americans are now ready to learn to live with the virus.
sentences.zh: 民主党官员告诉《泰晤士报》，这种变化反映了他们的信念，即越来越多的美国人现在准备好学会与病毒共存了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《泰晤士报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，去探索《泰晤士报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《泰晤士报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载该应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the Biden administration took its latest step to weaken Russia's hand in the growing standoff over Ukraine by acting to strengthen the position of U.S.
sentences.zh: 周二，拜登政府采取了最新举措，通过加强美国在欧洲盟友的地位，来削弱俄罗斯在乌克兰日益紧张的对峙中的筹码。

sentences.en: allies in Europe.
sentences.zh: 盟友在欧洲。

sentences.en: For weeks, European countries have worried that punishing Russia for possibly invading Ukraine
sentences.zh: 几周来，欧洲国家一直担心，因俄罗斯可能入侵乌克兰而惩罚俄罗斯，

sentences.en: could prompt Russia to punish Europe by cutting off crucial supplies of oil and gas in the dead of winter.
sentences.zh: 可能会促使俄罗斯通过在隆冬时节切断关键的石油和天然气供应来惩罚欧洲。

sentences.en: To alleviate those fears, the White House said it was working with oil and gas producers from the Middle East, North Africa, and Asia
sentences.zh: 为了缓解这些担忧，白宫表示正在与中东、北非和亚洲的石油和天然气生产商合作，

sentences.en: to ensure that European countries would have enough fuel even if Russia carried out that threat.
sentences.zh: 以确保即使俄罗斯实施了这一威胁，欧洲国家也有足够的燃料。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Russia engaged in its own act of provocation on Tuesday, conducting a wave of military exercises involving troops, tanks, and ballistic missiles,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，俄罗斯周二采取了自己的挑衅行动，进行了一波涉及军队、坦克和弹道导弹的军事演习，

sentences.en: many of them near its borders with Ukraine, in a deliberate show of its military might.
sentences.zh: 其中许多演习地点靠近其与乌克兰的边界，这是对其军事力量的蓄意展示。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung, Mooj Sadie, and Luke Vanderplug.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟、穆吉·萨迪和卢克·范德普拉格制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Anita Badajil, John Ketchum, Larissa Anderson, and Paige Cowett, contains original music by Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Corey Schreppel.
sentences.zh: 由安妮塔·巴达吉尔、约翰·凯彻姆、拉丽莎·安德森和佩奇·考特编辑，包含马里昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，并由科里·施雷佩尔进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landfork.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰德福克创作。

sentences.en: Of Wunderland.
sentences.zh: 来自Wunderland。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》节目中，我是莎拉·凯尼格，我们将讲述一些人试图维持自身影响力，却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
